First template per kind becomes default.

operations.operation: Read the owner's policy, or one section
operations.notes: Sections decision, eligibility, writing (scope cv, letter or all) and facts, each with its own version. An item with confirmed=false is a proposal or a value copied from the old Profile. The whole policy also lists the signals a decision rule may name; signals_applied is false until ingest computes them.

operations.operation: Add a policy item
operations.dashboard: Policy: Add a rule / Add a fact
operations.notes: expected_version is the section's version; a stale one returns 409 with details.current_version. Label, statement, optional typed value (text, number, date, boolean, list), note, scope (writing) and rule (decision). An agent token's item is a proposal until the owner confirms it. Optional idempotency_key.

operations.operation: Edit a policy item
operations.notes: expected_version is the section's version; a stale one returns 409 with details.current_version. Omitted fields stay; value, scope and rule accept null. A content change by the owner confirms the item; by an agent token it makes the item a proposal again and switches its rule off. Enabling a rule needs owner authority (403 forbidden for an agent token).

operations.operation: Move a policy item to another section
operations.notes: expected_version is the version of the item's section and target_version the version of the section it moves to. The item goes to the end; its confirmation stays. An item with a signal rule stays in decision.

operations.operation: Reorder a section's policy items
operations.notes: expected_version is the section's version; a stale one returns 409 with details.current_version. item_ids names every item of the section once, in the new order.

operations.operation: Confirm a proposed policy item
operations.notes: expected_version is the section's version; a stale one returns 409 with details.current_version. Confirms the item as it stands and records who confirmed it. An agent proposes and asks; it never confirms.

operations.operation: Remove a policy item
operations.notes: expected_version is the section's version; a stale one returns 409 with details.current_version. Frozen contexts retain their exact copies.

operations.operation: Search/filter/sort paginated application summaries
operations.notes: q, job_id, status, outcome (accepted/rejected/not_pursued/no_response), company, readiness (blocked/none/missing_pdf/unreviewed/reviewed/ready), ready (marked ready or not), no_reply_due (Applied longer than the no-reply period), ready_since, ready_until, applied_since, applied_until, sort (updated/newest/oldest/company/stage/applied/deadline/priority/ready), limit, offset; job_id is exact; stage_counts and ready_count span all matching records. readiness=ready is the stored Ready step; reviewed passes every check but is not marked ready. Rows include priority, deadline, readiness, ready_at, ready_by, concluded_on, last_response and unresolved/blocking requirement counts; full requirements are on the attempt read. no_reply gives the period in days, its source (the policy's No reply decision item, confirmed or not, or the 30-day default) and the number of Applied applications past it (due).

operations.operation: Read full attempt, questions/answers, requirements and job
operations.notes: readiness is derived from current revision leaves and unresolved blocking requirements; ready is reported only for an application marked ready (ready_at, ready_by) whose checks still pass.

operations.operation: Start application preparation (draft)
operations.notes: At most one non-Closed attempt per job. A conflicting new request reports the active application ID; idempotency keys support retries. Starting retains saved interest and leaves the pending Shortlist queue; it never submits or generates documents. Optional priority (1 highest to 5), deadline (YYYY-MM-DD) and structured employer requirements.

operations.operation: Record stage, outcome, priority, deadline, employer requirements, questions/answers and application instructions
operations.dashboard: Applications: progress, planning, requirements and questions/answers
operations.notes: expected_version prevents lost updates; recorded state changes create lifecycle history. Entering Closed requires an explicit outcome: accepted, rejected, not_pursued or no_response (no answer within the no-reply period; only for a sent application, with concluded_on, today by default). Moving to Interview or Offer, or closing as rejected (or accepted without an offer on record) records the matching employer response, dated response_date (today by default) with response_note; a response of that kind on that day is never repeated, and its date stays correctable with responses.update. Reopening enforces one open attempt per job. applied_at, priority or deadline null clears the value. requirements replaces the whole list; keep existing ids. The returned job is the compact job summary. Leaving Preparing or adding/unresolving a blocking requirement clears the stored Ready step.

operations.operation: Mark a Preparing application ready to apply, or clear the mark
operations.dashboard: Applications: Mark ready / Not ready in the attempt; Ready badge, filter and queue
operations.notes: expected_version; ready (default true). Refused with 409 application_not_ready and details.check (stage, blocked, none, missing_pdf, unreviewed) while a check fails. Cleared automatically, with an attributed application_ready_cleared event and its reason, by a new revision or context, a deleted revision, a file added to a current revision, a blocking requirement, or leaving Preparing. Never submits anything.

operations.operation: Delete one attempt and its owned history/files
operations.notes: expected_version is required. Keeps the archived job and other attempts; removes owned contexts/documents and their transfers.

operations.operation: Close, reopen, mark ready, unmark ready or delete selected application attempts
operations.notes: At most 200 versioned items, with per-item results/errors. Close requires an outcome (no_response only for sent applications, concluded today; rejected records a rejection response dated today); reopen requires a non-Closed stage and respects one open attempt per job. mark_ready is refused per item with application_not_ready while a readiness check fails.

List the employer responses of an application

operations.notes: Newest day first. Each response has kind (rejection, interview, offer, other), date, note, estimated (a day the 0.20 upgrade took from updated_at), origin (manual, stage or upgrade), version and created_by/updated_by. The application read also carries responses, and every list row its last_response.

operations.operation: Record an employer response to a sent application
operations.dashboard: Applications: Record response on an Applied, Interview or Offer row; Application review: Timeline, Record a response
operations.notes: kind, date (YYYY-MM-DD, not in the future), note and an optional idempotency_key. Only a sent application (applied_at, or Applied/Interview/Offer) accepts one: 409 application_not_sent otherwise. One response of a kind per day (409 response_exists with details.response_id); other may repeat. Never moves the stage: applications.update with response_date records the response together with the stage. An agent records only a response the owner reported.

operations.operation: Correct an employer response's kind, day or note
operations.dashboard: Application review: Timeline, Edit on a response

operations.operation: Read response, interview and offer rates of sent applications, overall and by group
operations.notes: Only employer responses count. Sent applications (applied_at, a sent stage or a response) form the sample; Drafts and attempts closed without being sent are counted under excluded, and agent dismissals are jobs, never applications. Rates are null with withheld below min_sample sent applications (default 5, 1 to 100); groups by role_family, seniority, location, source_kind, source and month applied; applied_since/applied_until narrow the sample by applied_at. Role family and seniority come from a keyword mapping of the job title (English, German, French, Italian).

exceptions.reason: Credential bootstrap and browser session transport precede authenticated domain tools; MCP uses bearer authentication. Logout revokes every browser session; API/MCP tokens remain valid.
Deployment liveness and service installation/startup are transport or operator concerns, not domain CRUD.
MCP initialization/discovery/session/resource transport is protocol infrastructure; no simulated dashboard button or MCP wrapper is required.
Shipped static reference files are convenience downloads, not private workspace records; agents may use REST or repository examples.

exceptions.dashboard: Read context/history; create new revisions or delete the owning attempt
exceptions.reason: Frozen contexts and lifecycle history have no arbitrary PATCH/DELETE. Document content changes create revisions; approved revisions stay immutable. Context deletion is scoped to deleting the owning application/job.
Logical file actions are equivalent across interfaces; raw HTTP bytes use scoped grants rather than base64 MCP payloads. Backup/export use their own scoped operational grants.
